Vivek / Sara — looping in logistics notes from our side.

Quick technical note: Google Calendar has a known "floating" time issue when an invite is forwarded or when the organizer's calendar is set to a different default timezone and the recipient's client assumes a floated event. Given DST starts in the US on 8 Mar 2026, some clients will shift. The safest approach is:

1) Create a new invite and set the event timezone explicitly to UTC (not just the organizer's local zone).
2) Add the meeting link in the body and attach the .ics as a fallback (some corporate clients ignore forwarded invites).
3) For EU attendees, if anyone is in CET/CEST, send them a separate invite created in Europe/Berlin timezone to avoid automatic DST rounding inconsistencies.

I'll draft the updated invite and send from our central calendar (lauren and I can create from europe/utc if needed).

Also — small ask for our ops team: if you could confirm the final attendee list and any required compliance paperwork (SOC2 evidence request was mentioned during discovery), we can include the right folks.

Thanks,
